title: GROUP BY: Summarizing by Categories 📦
description: Split your data into groups and apply aggregate functions to each group.

slides.title: Why Group? 🤔
slides.content:
# From Whole Table to Sub‑Groups

`GROUP BY` divides rows into sets based on a column (or columns). You then apply aggregate functions to each group independently.

Example: "Total sales per region" or "Average order by customer".

Syntax:
```sql
SELECT column, aggregate(column)
FROM table
GROUP BY column;
```

The column you group by must appear in the SELECT clause (unless it's inside an aggregate).

slides.title: Simple GROUP BY Example
slides.content:
Using our `orders` table:
```sql
SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS total_revenue
FROM orders
GROUP BY region;
```
This gives one row per region.

quizData.question: What happens if you SELECT a column that is not in GROUP BY nor inside an aggregate?

options.text: It returns the first value of that column per group
Most databases raise an error (unless it's functionally dependent)

quizData.explanation: Standard SQL requires all non‑aggregated columns in SELECT to be in GROUP BY.

slides.title: Multiple Aggregate Functions 🧮
slides.content:
You can compute several aggregates per group:

```sql
SELECT region,
       COUNT(*) AS num_orders,
       SUM(amount) AS total,
       AVG(amount) AS avg_order
FROM orders
GROUP BY region;
```

slides.title: Multi‑Aggregate Group
slides.content: Run this against sample data to see per‑region stats.
slides.codeSnippet: SELECT region, COUNT(*), SUM(amount), AVG(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY region;

quizData.question: What does `SELECT customer, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer;` show?
quizData.explanation: It groups rows by customer and counts rows in each group.

slides.title: GROUP BY Multiple Columns 🧩
slides.content:
## Hierarchical Grouping

```sql
SELECT region, customer, SUM(amount) AS total_spent
FROM orders
GROUP BY region, customer;
```

Now you get one row per unique (region, customer) combination.

slides.title: Two‑Column Group
slides.content: Total spending per customer per region:
slides.codeSnippet: SELECT region, customer, SUM(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY region, customer ORDER BY region, customer;

quizData.question: If you `GROUP BY A, B`, how many rows are returned?

options.text: Same as number of unique values in A
Number of unique combinations of A and B

quizData.explanation: Each distinct pair (A, B) gets its own row.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## GROUP BY 1,2 Shortcut

You can use column positions: `GROUP BY 1,2` groups by the first and second columns in SELECT. But it's brittle if the column order changes.

slides.title: Group By Practice 🏋️
slides.content:
Using the `orders` table:
1. Show total revenue per customer.
2. Show average order amount per region.
3. Show number of orders per region and customer (combine).
